$$\sigma^{2}={\sum_{i=1}^{N}(x_{i}-\bar{x})^{2}\over {N - 1}}$$ ::: ::: {.column width="70%"} ![](img/varianza3.png){width="100%"} ::: :::: ## ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](08-bivariada1_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Varianza educación {style="font-size: 0.75em;"} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} $$Varianza=\sigma^{2}={\sum_{i=1}^{N}(x_{i}-\bar{x})^{2}\over {N - 1}}$$ ::: {style="font-size: 1.3em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mean(data$educ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 5.125 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.3em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data$mean_educ <- mean(data$educ) data$dif_m_educ <- data$educ-data$mean_educ data$dif_m_educ2 <- (data$dif_m_educ)^2 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .fragment width="50%"} ::: {style="font-size: 1.3em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} kbl(data, digits = 2) %>% scroll_box(width = "500px", height = "500px") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

::: {style="font-size: 1.6em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} var(data$ing) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 11.41071 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: :::: ## ¿Por qué es importante la **varianza**? {data-background-color="#0C3547"}

````` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="65%"} Graficando cada caso: ![](img/educ-ing5.png){width="80%" fig-align="center"} ::: :::: ## En R {style="font-size: 0.8em;"} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"} ::: {style="font-size: 1.3em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot1 <- ggplot(data, aes(x=educ, y=ing)) + geom_point( colour = "red", size = 5) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8, limits = c(1, 8)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:12, limits = c(1, 12)) + theme(text = element_text(size = 20)) ``` ::: ::: ::: Nube de puntos: ::: {.column width="65%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](08-bivariada1_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=432} ::: ::: ::: :::: ## [La **nube de puntos** o scatterplot es una representación gráfica de la asociación de dos variables, donde cada punto representa el valor de cada caso en cada una de las variables]{style="color: white;"} {data-background-color="#0C3547"} ## :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="35%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](08-bivariada1_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){width=432} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="45%"}

::: {.content-box-red} ¿Cómo expresar matemáticamente este patrón de asociación? ::: ::: :::: # [2. Covarianza]{style="color: white;"} {data-background-color="#0C3547"} ## Hacia la covarianza {style="font-size: 0.8em;"} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](08-bivariada1_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-17-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {style="text-align: center;"} [Educación]{style="font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: bold;"} ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](08-bivariada1_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-18-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {style="text-align: center;"} [Ingreso]{style="font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: bold;"} ::: ::: :::: ## Covarianza {style="font-size: 0.8em;"} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {style="text-align: center;"} [Varianza educación (x)]{style="font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: bold;"} $$\sigma_{edu}^{2}={\sum_{i=1}^{N}(x_{i}-\bar{x})^{2}\over {N - 1}}$$ $$\sigma_{edu}^{2}={\sum_{i=1}^{N}(x_{i}-\bar{x})(x_{i}-\bar{x})\over {N - 1}}$$ ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {style="text-align: center;"} [Varianza ingreso (y)]{style="font-size: 1.3em; font-weight: bold;"} $$\sigma_{ing}^{2}={\sum_{i=1}^{N}(y_{i}-\bar{y})^{2}\over {N - 1}}$$ $$\sigma_{ing}^{2}={\sum_{i=1}^{N}(y_{i}-\bar{y})(y_{i}-\bar{y})\over {N - 1}}$$ ::: ::: :::: ::: {.content-box-red .fragment} $$Covarianza=cov(x,y) = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(x_i - \bar{x})(y_i - \bar{y})} {N-1}$$ ::: ## Cálculo covarianza {style="font-size: 0.75em;"} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {style="font-size: 1.3em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data$dif_xy <- data$dif_m_educ* data$dif_m_ing ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.3em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data %>% select(educ,ing, dif_m_educ, dif_m_ing, dif_xy) %>% kbl ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column .fragment width="60%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
educ ing dif_m_educ dif_m_ing dif_xy
2 1 -3.125 -4.375 13.671875
3 3 -2.125 -2.375 5.046875
4 3 -1.125 -2.375 2.671875
4 5 -1.125 -0.375 0.421875
5 4 -0.125 -1.375 0.171875
7 7 1.875 1.625 3.046875
8 9 2.875 3.625 10.421875
8 11 2.875 5.625 16.171875
````` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.3em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sum(data$dif_xy) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 51.625 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Covarianza {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} $$ \begin{align*} Covarianza=cov(x,y) &= \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_i - \bar{x})(y_i - \bar{y})} {N-1} \\ &= \frac{51.625} {8-1} \\ &=7.375 \end{align*} $$ ::: {style="font-size: 1.3em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cov(data$educ,data$ing) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 7.375 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## {data-background-color="#0C3547"} ::: {style="color: white; font-size: 1em;"} - La [covarianza]{style="color: #dfc117;"} es una medida de asociación entre variables basada en la variabilidad de cada una de ellas - La distancia del promedio del valor de una variable (residuo): ¿tiene relación con el residuo de otra variable? - Expresa la medida en que los valores de cada variable se distancian respectivamente de su promedio - [Su valor no es interpretable directamente]{style="color: #dfc117;"} ::: # [3. Correlación de Pearson]{style="color: white;"} {data-background-color="#0C3547"} ## Correlación producto-momento de Pearson {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="30%"} ![](img/pearson.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: {.column width="70%"}
- Medida estandarizada de covarianza - Basada en los trabajos de Galton y de Bravais - Desarrollada por Karl Pearson (1857-1936): físico, matemático, estadístico y germanista. Y eugenista ... ::: :::: ## Correlación producto-momento (Pearson): _r_ {style="font-size: 0.8em;"} $$ \begin{align*} Covarianza = cov(x,y) &= \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_i - \bar{x})(y_i - \bar{y})} {n-1}\\ \\ Correlación=r &= \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_i - \bar{x})(y_i - \bar{y})} {(n-1)\sigma_x \sigma_y }\\ \\ &= \frac{\sum(x-\bar{x})(y-\bar{y})}{\sqrt{\sum(x-\bar{x})^{2} \sum(y-\bar{y})^{2}}} \end{align*} $$ ## Cálculo correlación r de Pearson {style="font-size: 0.75em;"} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
educ ing dif_m_educ2 dif_m_ing2 dif_xy
2 1 9.77 19.14 13.67
3 3 4.52 5.64 5.05
4 3 1.27 5.64 2.67
4 5 1.27 0.14 0.42
5 4 0.02 1.89 0.17
7 7 3.52 2.64 3.05
8 9 8.27 13.14 10.42
8 11 8.27 31.64 16.17
````` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} $$r=\frac{\sum(x-\bar{x})(y-\bar{y})}{\sqrt{\sum(x-\bar{x})^{2} \sum(y-\bar{y})^{2}}}$$ ::: {style="font-size: 1.3em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sum(data$dif_xy); sum(data$dif_m_educ2);sum(data$dif_m_ing2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 51.625 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 36.875 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 79.875 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Cálculo correlación {style="font-size: 0.8em;"} :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} $$ \begin{align*} r &= \frac{\sum(x-\bar{x})(y-\bar{y})}{\sqrt{\sum(x-\bar{x})^{2} \sum(y-\bar{y})^{2}}} \\ \\ &= \frac{51.625}{ \sqrt{36.875*79.875}} \\ \\ &= \frac{51.625}{54.271} \\ \\ &= 0.951 \end{align*} $$ ::: ::: {.column .fragment width="45%"} ::: {style="font-size: 1.3em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cor(data$educ,data$ing) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.9512367 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Interpretación {data-background-color="#9B2626"} ::: {style="color: white;"} - El coeficiente de correlación (de Pearson) es una medida de asociación lineal entre variables, que indica el sentido y la fuerza de la asociación - Varía entre +1 y -1, donde - valores **positivos** indican relación directa (aumenta una, aumenta la otra) - valores **negativos** indican relación inversa (aumenta una, disminuye la otra) ::: ## Nubes de puntos (scatterplot) ![](img/scatters.png){fig-align="center"} ## Nubes de puntos (scatterplot) ![](img/scatters2.png){fig-align="center"} ## Nubes de puntos (scatterplot) ![](img/scatters3.png){fig-align="center"} ## Adivine la correlación: {style="text-align: center;"} ### [guessthecorrelation.com](https://www.guessthecorrelation.com) ## Nubes de puntos (scatterplot) ![](img/scatters4.png){fig-align="center"} # [4. Limitaciones]{style="color: white;"} {data-background-color="#0C3547"} ## Limitaciones correlación - medida de asociación [lineal]{style="color: #c0392b;"} entre variables - no captura apropiadamente asociaciones no lineales - posee supuestos distribucionales de x e y (distribución normal) - sensible a valores extremos - un mismo coeficiente puede reflejar distintas distribuciones bivariadas ## ![](img/anscombe.png){width="80%" fig-align="center"} # [Resumen]{style="color: #dfc117;"} {data-background-color="#0C3547"} ::: {style="color: white; font-size: 1.2em;"} - Asociación, explicación y ciencias sociales - Varianza y covarianza - Pearson: asociación en un número en rango fijo ::: ## Recomendación :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="40%"} ![](img/Alice_Lee.jpg){width="90%" fig-align="center"} ::: ::: {.column width="60%"}
[Alice Lee: Correlación, inteligencia y tamaño del cráneo en hombres y mujeres](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Lee) ::: :::: # {.hide-logo data-background-color="#0C3547"}
